metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 5–10 day horizons.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model may lag in adjusting; add 1–3 day lag correction to forecast decline.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–30 day horizons; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in the horizon; apply 5–10% downward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment is positive and price is falling, model may misread trend; reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
